subject: Cascade Health — request for extended log archival and deletion exception
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@cascadehealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: David Li <david.li@cascadehealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: extended log archival for upcoming compliance audit

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Cascade Health is preparing for a multi-year HIPAA audit and our compliance team surfaced a hard requirement: certain access and event logs must be retained and tamper-evident for up to 7 years. Specifically they called out: authentication logs, admin role changes, record-access audit trails and system configuration change events.

We reviewed Redwood's standard documentation but need confirmation on three items before the audit memo is finalized:
- Can Redwood retain the specified logs for 7 years under contract?
- If yes, will logs be stored in a manner that supports integrity verification (signed manifests / append-only storage / object versioning)?
- What proof/evidence can Redwood provide during an audit (SOC 2 attestation section, signed export, CAIQ responses)?

Attached is a redacted compliance summary from our security team (HIPAA_audit_requirements.pdf) that highlights the clauses. We are open to either Redwood hosting a longer-term archive (if feasible) or Redwood streaming encrypted logs to a customer-managed S3 bucket with retention settings we control.

We need a short write-up and a proposed contractual addendum by EOD Tuesday — the audit scheduling is tight. Please advise next steps and who we should loop in.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Compliance | Cascade Health

---
Note: this email contains redacted PHI examples for the compliance review.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@cascadehealth.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended log archival for upcoming compliance audit

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and for the summary. I appreciate the timeline pressure; we can move quickly. Per your three bullets:

1) Retention duration: our hosted default for security/audit logs is 365 days. For >365 days we offer two supported approaches: (a) Dedicated/Private deployments where we can configure archival retention to your requirement, or (b) secure log export to a customer-controlled cloud bucket (recommended for hosted customers).

2) Integrity and tamper evidence: we support object versioning + write-once bucket policies on S3 as a standard approach. For Redwood-managed archives we can provide signed manifests and SHA256 digests. Full append-only storage with independent attestation is generally available as an add-on for enterprise contracts and requires a short implementation window.

3) Evidence for audit: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report (redacted in parts), CAIQ responses for logging controls, and a signed export of the retained logs for the requested timeframe.

Next steps I propose: Rishi will confirm the technical feasibility for hosted customers and sketch an approach (streaming vs. Redwood-hosted archive); Neha will prepare a short commercial addendum (scope, pricing, contract language) we can share with legal; I will draft a one-page summary for your auditors. Rishi/Neha — can you weigh in? Olivia — if you prefer an S3 export, please share the bucket policy and retention/Governance SLOs you need.

I attached our high-level whitepaper on log archival options (redwood_log_archival_whitepaper.pdf).

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@cascadehealth.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended log archival for upcoming compliance audit

Hi all — quick technical note on options and constraints. I ran this by the infra team overnight. TL;DR: we can meet Cascade's request, but the implementation path depends on deployment mode.

Option A — Hosted customer + Redwood-managed archive:
- We can store a segregated encrypted archive for selected log streams for multi-year retention (7 years).
- Integrity: we create monthly signed manifests (SHA256) and store them alongside the archive; we retain object versioning and enable immutable retention windows.
- Caveats: for hosted tenants we keep an indexed search layer for 365 days (for latency/operational reasons). After 365 days, logs are kept as compressed archived blobs with slower retrieval (24-72h) and charged egress/restore fees. This is an enterprise add-on and requires an SLA amendment.

Option B — Customer-managed bucket (recommended for speed/evidence):
- We can stream logs in near-real time to an S3-compatible endpoint you control, using TLS + mTLS.
- We support server-side encryption keys managed by the customer (SSE-C/KMS) and can add object-lock (governance mode) to prevent deletion.
- We sign each upload and can provide a signed manifest monthly for your records.

Operational details:
- Log types supported: auth events, admin role changes, record access events, system config diffs.
- Searchability: exported archives are raw; we can provide optional index exports for up to 1 year of logs to aid investigations.
- Legal hold: we can implement a legal-hold flag to prevent automated lifecycle pruning.

Pilot offer: I can set up a 30-day pilot to stream a subset of log types to a test S3 bucket and demonstrate manifest verification. Timing: we can start within 5 business days after contract addendum.

Olivia — if you want the hosted archive route we will need a signed MSA addendum and a short implementation window (2-3 weeks). If you want fast evidence for the auditors, pick Option B and share the bucket endpoint/policy.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the manifest format and the verification steps.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@cascadehealth.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended log archival for upcoming compliance audit

Thanks Rishi — clear options. Olivia, to keep the audit timeline, we recommend Option B (customer-managed bucket). Neha will draft the "Logs Retention Addendum" with two short paragraphs: scope of logs, retention duration (7 years), evidence deliverables (monthly signed manifests + one-time full export), and fees for long-term storage/egress.

Neha, could you draft language for the addendum and include pricing assumptions? Also flag any terms that need legal review (indemnity, export format, restore SLA). I added Markus to review given the 7-year retention and pricing sensitivity.

Olivia — if you send the S3 endpoint and the minimal bucket policy we need (we prefer an IAM role trust rather than a shared key), Rishi and I will kick off the pilot as soon as the addendum is signed.

Appreciate the urgency — we will target delivery of the draft addendum today for your review.

—Marissa
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@cascadehealth.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended log archival for upcoming compliance audit

I've reviewed the proposed approach. Approved to proceed with Option B (customer-managed bucket) as the default for hosted accounts requesting multi-year retention. Please ensure the addendum includes: (1) explicit mention of who bears restore/egress costs, (2) a clause about our right to suspend streaming if the bucket policy is misconfigured, and (3) requirement for customer proof of immutable storage (object-lock governance) for audit evidence.

Marissa/Neha — proceed with the addendum draft and loop Legal if anything in indemnity/external storage looks risky.

-Markus
